extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and Principal Investigators preparing NSF grant proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing the Broader Impacts (BI) section of NSF research proposals, and the review criteria reviewers use to evaluate BI statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The potential to benefit society and contribute to the achievement of specific, desired societal outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF expects researchers' work to have broader impacts that meaningfully benefit society and advance defined societal goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 1 — Potential to benefit society or advance desired societal outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the potential for the proposed activity to benefit society or advance desired societal outcomes?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess the concrete ways the proposed activity could produce societal benefits or advance specified outcomes; tie activities to measurable or observable benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 2 — Creativity and transformative potential
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent do the proposed activities suggest and explore creative, original or potentially transformative concepts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether activities are innovative or exploratory in ways that could lead to transformative societal impacts rather than only routine efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 3 — Quality of the plan and assessment mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the plan for carrying out the proposed activities well-reasoned, well-organized and based on sound rationale? Does the plan incorporate a mechanism to assess success?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a clear, logical implementation plan and an evaluation/assessment component so reviewers can judge feasibility and how impact will be measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 4 — Qualifications to carry out the activities
rubrics_metrics.description: How well qualified is the individual, team or institution to conduct the proposed activities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate relevant experience, expertise, or partnerships that show the PI/team/institution can successfully implement the BI activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 5 — Adequacy of resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there adequate resources available to the principal investigator to carry out the proposed activities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document available infrastructure, personnel, funding, and institutional support necessary to carry out and sustain the proposed BI activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: How Broader Impacts Can Be Accomplished
rubrics_metrics.description: Broader impacts may be achieved through multiple modes: through the research itself; through activities directly related to specific research projects; or through activities supported by, but complementary to, the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the BI will arise naturally from the research outcomes, will be implemented as project-integrated activities (e.g., outreach tied to experiments), or will be complementary activities (e.g., separate training programs funded alongside the research).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of Desired Societal Outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative outcomes NSF considers desirable, such as improving STEM education, increasing public scientific literacy, improving well-being, building partnerships, and enhancing national competitiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these outcome examples to align BI goals: improving education and educator development in STEM; increasing public scientific literacy and engagement; improving well‑being of individuals in society; developing a globally competitive STEM workforce; building partnerships between academia, industry and others; improving national security; increasing U.S. economic competitiveness; enhancing infrastructure for research and education; increasing participation of underrepresented groups in STEM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Writing Tip — Be Specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't just say 'students will be trained in bioinformatics.' Give details: how many students, what type of students, how will they be recruited, trained, and evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete numbers, target populations, recruitment strategies, training methods, timelines, and evaluation metrics so reviewers can assess scale and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Writing Tip — Plan to Evaluate
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan to evaluate; have an evaluation plan in place to report impact at the end of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear assessment methods and metrics, describe data collection and analysis for measuring success, and explain how evaluation findings will be used for improvement and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Writing Tip — Identify Your Audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the intended community and match your strategy. If you propose an open-access tool that focuses on one part of society, ensure your tool is appropriate for that audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define the target audience(s) explicitly and tailor activities, dissemination, and evaluation to their needs and contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Writing Tip — Match Career Goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop an 'impact identity' matched with your career trajectory. Build sustained engagement rather than one-off activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how BI activities fit the PI's long-term professional development and how activities will be sustained or integrated into future work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Common Pitfalls
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitfalls to avoid when writing BI statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on generic education components expected of any PI (e.g., mentoring graduate students alone is not enough); don't promise more than you can deliver; don't treat BI as an afterthought; don't list activities without infrastructure to support them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common Broader Impacts Activity Categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical categories of BI activities that accomplish societal outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: 1) Education (K‑12 outreach, undergraduate research, graduate training); 2) Public engagement (museums, citizen science, media); 3) Workforce development (training, internships); 4) Diversity, equity, and inclusion (URM recruitment, accessibility); 5) Economic development (technology transfer, entrepreneurship); 6) Infrastructure (datasets, tools, instrumentation); 7) International collaboration; 8) Societal/ethical implications.
